text: The normal echocardiogram and rubella IgM results make Congenital Rubella Syndrome and significant congenital heart disease unlikely causes for the apnea. speaker: Doctor
text: The lack of jaundice or failure to thrive helps rule out several metabolic and infectious causes. Since the infant is 1 month old and was born prematurely, apnea is a common complication of immature respiratory control, but the anemia needs explanation; has the infant had any recent episodes of pallor, lethargy, or feeding difficulties associated with the low hemoglobin?

text:
The pale conjunctiva confirms significant anemia, which in a premature infant at this age is highly suggestive of anemia of prematurity due to suppressed erythropoiesis and frequent phlebotomy. I will check the complete blood count to assess the severity and reticulocyte count to evaluate bone marrow response.
